sanskrit: athābhiṣiṣicur droṇaṃ duryodhanamukhā nṛpāḥ senāpatye yathā skandaṃ purā śakramukhāḥ surāḥ
english: Then the kings, led by Duryodhana, consecrated Droṇa to the supreme command, even as the gods of old, led by Śakra, had consecrated Skanda.

sanskrit: tato vāditraghoṣeṇa saha puṃsāṃ mahāsvanaiḥ prādurāsīt kṛte droṇe harṣaḥ senāpatau tadā
english: Then, with the sound of musical instruments mingling with the mighty cries of the men, great joy arose when Droṇa was made commander of the host.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṇyāhaghoṣeṇa svastivādasvanena ca saṃstavair gītaśabdaiś ca sūtamāgadhabandinām
english: Then with the proclamation of the auspicious day and the chant of benediction, with the praises and the songs of the bards, the heralds, and the panegyrists,

sanskrit: jayaśabdair dvijāgryāṇāṃ subhagānartitais tathā satkṛtya vidhivad droṇaṃ jitān manyanta pāṇḍavān
english: and with the victory-cries of the foremost brāhmaṇas and the dances of fair women, they honored Droṇa according to rite, and deemed the Pāṇḍavas already vanquished.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca senāpatyaṃ tu saṃprāpya bhāradvājo mahārathaḥ yuyutsur vyūhya sainyāni prāyāt tava sutaiḥ saha
english: Saṃjaya said: Having attained the supreme command, the son of Bharadvāja, that mighty car-warrior, eager for battle, marshaled the troops in array and advanced together with your sons.

sanskrit: saindhavaś ca kaliṅgaś ca vikarṇaś ca tavātmajaḥ dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvam āsthāya samatiṣṭhanta daṃśitāḥ
english: The lord of the Sindhus, the king of the Kaliṅgas, and Vikarṇa your son took their stand upon the right flank, clad in armor.

sanskrit: prapakṣaḥ śakunis teṣāṃ pravarair hayasādibhiḥ yayau gāndhārakaiḥ sārdhaṃ vimalaprāsayodhibhiḥ
english: As their outer wing, Śakuni advanced with his choice horsemen, together with the men of Gāndhāra, warriors armed with bright lances.

sanskrit: kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca citraseno viviṃśatiḥ duḥśāsanamukhā yattāḥ savyaṃ pārśvam apālayan
english: Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman, Citrasena, and Viviṃśati, led by Duḥśāsana and on the alert, guarded the left flank.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prapakṣāḥ kāmbojāḥ sudakṣiṇapuraḥsarāḥ yayur aśvair mahāvegaiḥ śakāś ca yavanaiḥ saha
english: As their outer wing, the Kāmbojas, with Sudakṣiṇa at their head, advanced on swift-flying horses, along with the Śakas and the Yavanas.

sanskrit: madrās trigartāḥ sāmbaṣṭhāḥ pratīcyodīcyavāsinaḥ śibayaḥ śūrasenāś ca śūdrāś ca maladaiḥ saha
english: The Madras, the Trigartas, the Ambaṣṭhas, the dwellers of the west and the north, the Śibis and the Śūrasenas, the Śūdras together with the Maladas,

sanskrit: sauvīrāḥ kitavāḥ prācyā dākṣiṇātyāś ca sarvaśaḥ tavātmajaṃ puraskṛtya sūtaputrasya pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: the Sauvīras, the Kitavas, the easterners and the southerners, every one of them, placing your son at their head, marched behind the son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: harṣayan sarvasainyāni baleṣu balam ādadhat yayau vaikartanaḥ karṇaḥ pramukhe sarvadhanvinām
english: Gladdening all the troops and lending strength to the strong, Karṇa the son of Vikartana advanced at the forefront of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: tasya dīpto mahākāyaḥ svāny anīkāni harṣayan hastikakṣyāmahāketur babhau sūryasamadyutiḥ
english: His great banner, blazing and huge of body, bearing the device of an elephant's girth and gladdening his own divisions, shone with a splendor equal to the sun's.

sanskrit: na bhīṣmavyasanaṃ kaś cid dṛṣṭvā karṇam amanyata viśokāś cābhavan sarve rājānaḥ kurubhiḥ saha
english: Beholding Karṇa, not one reckoned the calamity of Bhīṣma's fall; and all the kings, together with the Kurus, became free of grief.

sanskrit: hṛṣṭāś ca bahavo yodhās tatrājalpanta saṃgatāḥ na hi karṇaṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā yudhi sthāsyanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: And many of the warriors, gathered together and rejoicing, spoke thus among themselves: 'When once they behold Karṇa in the fray, the Pāṇḍavas will not stand their ground in battle.'

sanskrit: karṇo hi samare śakto jetuṃ devān savāsavān kim u pāṇḍusutān yuddhe hīnavīryaparākramān
english: 'For Karṇa is able in combat to vanquish the gods themselves, with Vāsava at their head—how much more the sons of Pāṇḍu, whose valor and might are now diminished in war.'

sanskrit: bhīṣmeṇa tu raṇe pārthāḥ pālitā bāhuśālinā tāṃs tu karṇaḥ śarais tīkṣṇair nāśayiṣyaty asaṃśayam
english: 'The sons of Pṛthā were shielded in battle by the mighty-armed Bhīṣma; but Karṇa with his sharp shafts will destroy them, beyond all doubt.'

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvantas te 'nyonyaṃ hṛṣṭarūpā viśāṃ pate rādheyaṃ pūjayantaś ca praśaṃsantaś ca niryayuḥ
english: Speaking thus to one another, joyful of countenance, O lord of peoples, honoring and praising the son of Rādhā, they marched forth.

sanskrit: asmākaṃ śakaṭavyūho droṇena vihito 'bhavat pareṣāṃ krauñca evāsīd vyūho rājan mahātmanām prīyamāṇena vihito dharmarājena bhārata
english: Ours was the wagon-array, formed by Droṇa; but the array of the high-souled foe was the heron, O king—formed in delight by the King of Righteousness, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: vyūhapramukhatas teṣāṃ tasthatuḥ puruṣarṣabhau vānaradhvajam ucchritya viṣvaksenadhanaṃjayau
english: At the front of their array stood those two bulls among men, Viṣvaksena and Dhanaṃjaya, raising aloft the ape-bannered standard.

sanskrit: kakudaṃ sarvasainyānāṃ lakṣma sarvadhanuṣmatām ādityapathagaḥ ketuḥ pārthasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: The standard of Pārtha of measureless splendor—the summit of all the hosts, the ensign of all the bowmen—ranged along the very path of the sun.

sanskrit: dīpayām āsa tat sainyaṃ pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ yathā prajvalitaḥ sūryo yugānte vai vasuṃdharām
english: It set ablaze that army of the high-souled Pāṇḍava, as the blazing sun at the dissolution of an age sets the whole earth aflame.

sanskrit: asyatām arjunaḥ śreṣṭho gāṇḍīvaṃ dhanuṣāṃ varam vāsudevaś ca bhūtānāṃ cakrāṇāṃ ca sudarśanam
english: Among archers Arjuna is supreme, among bows the Gāṇḍīva is foremost, among beings Vāsudeva, and among discuses the Sudarśana.

sanskrit: catvāry etāni tejāṃsi vahañ śvetahayo rathaḥ pareṣām agratas tasthau kālacakram ivodyatam
english: Bearing these four splendors, the white-horsed chariot stood before the foe like the uplifted wheel of Time.

sanskrit: evam etau mahātmānau balasenāgragāv ubhau tāvakānāṃ mukhaṃ karṇaḥ pareṣāṃ ca dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Thus these two great-souled ones both stood at the vanguard of their armies: Karṇa the front of your host, and Dhanaṃjaya that of the foe.

sanskrit: tato jātābhisaṃrambhau parasparavadhaiṣiṇau avekṣetāṃ tadānyonyaṃ samare karṇapāṇḍavau
english: Then, both kindled to fury and each seeking the other's death, Karṇa and the Pāṇḍava gazed upon one another in the field of battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ prayāte sahasā bhāradvāje mahārathe antarnādena ghoreṇa vasudhā samakampata
english: Then, as the mighty car-warrior, the son of Bharadvāja, suddenly advanced, the earth trembled with a terrible inner roar.

sanskrit: tatas tumulam ākāśam āvṛṇot sadivākaram vātoddhūtaṃ rajas tīvraṃ kauśeyanikaropamam
english: Then a fierce dust, raised up by the wind and tumultuous, like a heap of silken cloth, veiled the sky together with the sun.

sanskrit: anabhre pravavarṣa dyaur māṃsāsthirudhirāṇy uta gṛdhrāḥ śyenā baḍāḥ kaṅkā vāyasāś ca sahasraśaḥ upary upari senāṃ te tadā paryapatan nṛpa
english: From a cloudless heaven there rained down flesh and bones and blood; and vultures, hawks, herons, kites, and crows by the thousand then wheeled circling above the host, O king.

sanskrit: gomāyavaś ca prākrośan bhayadān dāruṇān ravān akārṣur apasavyaṃ ca bahuśaḥ pṛtanāṃ tava cikhādiṣanto māṃsāni pipāsantaś ca śoṇitam
english: Jackals howled dreadful, fear-bringing cries, and again and again circled your army from the left, hungering to devour the flesh and thirsting for the blood.

sanskrit: apatad dīpyamānā ca sanirghātā sakampanā ulkā jvalantī saṃgrāme pucchenāvṛtya sarvaśaḥ
english: And there fell a blazing meteor, flaming, attended by thunderclaps and tremors, veiling the whole field of battle on every side with its tail of fire.

sanskrit: pariveṣo mahāṃś cāpi savidyutstanayitnumān bhāskarasyābhavad rājan prayāte vāhinīpatau
english: And a great halo, attended by lightning and thunder, appeared about the sun, O king, as the lord of the host advanced.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ prādurāsan sudāruṇāḥ utpātā yudhi vīrāṇāṃ jīvitakṣayakārakāḥ
english: These and many other most dreadful portents arose, foretelling in the war the destruction of the heroes' lives.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ parasparavadhaiṣiṇām kurupāṇḍavasainyānāṃ śabdenānādayaj jagat
english: Then began the battle of the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, each seeking the other's death, making the world resound with its din.

sanskrit: te tv anyonyaṃ susaṃrabdhāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ kauravaiḥ saha pratyaghnan niśitair bāṇair jayagṛddhāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: Greatly enraged at one another, the Pāṇḍavas with the Kauravas, those smiters greedy for victory, struck back with whetted shafts.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍavānāṃ mahatīṃ maheṣvāso mahādyutiḥ vegenābhyadravat senāṃ kirañ śaraśataiḥ śitaiḥ
english: That mighty bowman of great splendor rushed with speed upon the great army of the Pāṇḍavas, scattering hundreds of sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: droṇam abhyudyataṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavāḥ saha sṛñjayaiḥ pratyagṛhṇaṃs tadā rājañ śaravarṣaiḥ pṛthak pṛthak
english: Seeing Droṇa thus risen against them, the Pāṇḍavas together with the Sṛñjayas received him then, O king, each in his turn, with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: saṃkṣobhyamāṇā droṇena bhidyamānā mahācamūḥ vyaśīryata sapāñcālā vāteneva balāhakāḥ
english: Shaken and rent asunder by Droṇa, the great host with the Pāñcālas was scattered like banks of cloud before the wind.

sanskrit: bahūnīha vikurvāṇo divyāny astrāṇi saṃyuge apīḍayat kṣaṇenaiva droṇaḥ pāṇḍavasṛñjayān
english: Wielding in that combat many celestial weapons, Droṇa in but a moment sorely oppressed the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā droṇena vāsaveneva dānavāḥ pāñcālāḥ samakampanta dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ
english: Slaughtered by Droṇa as the Dānavas by Vāsava, the Pāñcālas, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head, trembled.

sanskrit: tato divyāstravic chūro yājñasenir mahārathaḥ abhinac charavarṣeṇa droṇānīkam anekadhā
english: Then the hero, the son of Yajñasena, that mighty car-warrior, skilled in celestial weapons, broke Droṇa's division asunder in many places with a shower of shafts.

sanskrit: droṇasya śaravarṣais tu śaravarṣāṇi bhāgaśaḥ saṃnivārya tataḥ senāṃ kurūn apy avadhīd balī
english: With his showers of shafts that powerful one warded off, part by part, the showers of Droṇa's arrows, and then slew the army of the Kurus as well.

sanskrit: saṃhṛtya tu tato droṇaḥ samavasthāpya cāhave svam anīkaṃ mahābāhuḥ pārṣataṃ samupādravat
english: Then Droṇa, the mighty-armed, having rallied and steadied his own division in the fray, rushed upon the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: sa bāṇavarṣaṃ sumahad asṛjat pārṣataṃ prati maghavān samabhikruddhaḥ sahasā dānaveṣv iva
english: He loosed a vast shower of arrows against the son of Pṛṣata, as Maghavan in sudden wrath against the Dānavas.

sanskrit: te kampyamānā droṇena bāṇaiḥ pāṇḍavasṛñjayāḥ punaḥ punar abhajyanta siṃhenevetare mṛgāḥ
english: Made to tremble by Droṇa's arrows, the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas broke and fled again and again, like lesser beasts before a lion.

sanskrit: atha paryapatad droṇaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ balaṃ balī alātacakravad rājaṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then the mighty Droṇa wheeled about through the army of the Pāṇḍavas like a whirling firebrand, O king, and that seemed a wondrous thing.

sanskrit: khacaranagarakalpaṃ kalpitaṃ śāstradṛṣṭyā; caladanilapatākaṃ hrādinaṃ valgitāśvam sphaṭikavimalaketuṃ tāpanaṃ śātravāṇāṃ; rathavaram adhirūḍhaḥ saṃjahārārisenām
english: Mounted upon his peerless chariot—like a city moving through the air, fashioned by the lore of scripture, its pennon fluttering in the shifting wind, thundering, its horses prancing, its standard pure as crystal, a scorcher of foes—he annihilated the army of his enemies.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā droṇam abhighnantaṃ sāśvasūtarathadvipān vyathitāḥ pāṇḍavā dṛṣṭvā na cainaṃ paryavārayan
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding Droṇa thus smiting their horses, charioteers, chariots, and elephants, the Pāṇḍavas were stricken with dread and could not hem him in.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā dhṛṣṭadyumnadhanaṃjayau abravīt sarvato yattaiḥ kumbhayonir nivāryatām
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira said to Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Dhanaṃjaya: 'Let the pitcher-born one be checked by men set on guard upon every side.'

sanskrit: tatrainam arjunaś caiva pārṣataś ca sahānugaḥ paryagṛhṇaṃs tataḥ sarve samāyāntaṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Thereupon Arjuna and the son of Pṛṣata with his followers, and then all the mighty car-warriors, hemmed in that advancing foe.

sanskrit: kekayā bhīmasenaś ca saubhadro 'tha ghaṭotkacaḥ yudhiṣṭhiro yamau matsyā drupadasyātmajās tathā
english: The Kekayas and Bhīmasena, the son of Subhadrā, and Ghaṭotkaca, Yudhiṣṭhira, the twins, the Matsyas, and the sons of Drupada,

sanskrit: draupadeyāś ca saṃhṛṣṭā dhṛṣṭaketuḥ sasātyakiḥ cekitānaś ca saṃkruddho yuyutsuś ca mahārathaḥ
english: the sons of Draupadī full of joy, Dhṛṣṭaketu with Sātyaki, the wrathful Cekitāna, and Yuyutsu the mighty car-warrior,

sanskrit: ye cānye pārthivā rājan pāṇḍavasyānuyāyinaḥ kulavīryānurūpāṇi cakruḥ karmāṇy anekaśaḥ
english: and whatever other princes, O king, were followers of the Pāṇḍava, wrought deeds in great number worthy of their lineage and their valor.

sanskrit: saṃgṛhyamāṇāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavair vāhinīṃ raṇe vyāvṛtya cakṣuṣī kopād bhāradvājo 'nvavaikṣata
english: Seeing his army being thus hemmed in by the Pāṇḍavas in the battle, the son of Bharadvāja, rolling his eyes in wrath, looked upon them.

sanskrit: sa tīvraṃ kopam āsthāya rathe samaradurmadaḥ vyadhamat pāṇḍavānīkam abhrāṇīva sadāgatiḥ
english: Yielding to fierce anger upon his chariot, that one furious in battle scattered the army of the Pāṇḍavas as the ever-moving wind scatters the clouds.

sanskrit: rathān aśvān narān nāgān abhidhāvaṃs tatas tataḥ cacāronmattavad droṇo vṛddho 'pi taruṇo yathā
english: Charging chariots, horses, men, and elephants this way and that, Droṇa ranged about as one frenzied, and, though aged, was as a youth.

sanskrit: tasya śoṇitadigdhāṅgāḥ śoṇās te vātaraṃhasaḥ ājāneyā hayā rājann avibhrāntāḥ śriyaṃ dadhuḥ
english: His red steeds, swift as the wind, of noble breed, their bodies smeared with blood, O king, unswerving, bore a surpassing splendor.

sanskrit: tam antakam iva kruddham āpatantaṃ yatavratam dṛṣṭvā saṃprādravan yodhāḥ pāṇḍavasya tatas tataḥ
english: Beholding that man of steadfast vow rushing upon them, wrathful as the Ender himself, the warriors of the Pāṇḍava fled in every direction.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ pradravatāṃ bhīmaḥ punar āvartatām api vīkṣatāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ cāsīc chabdaḥ paramadāruṇaḥ
english: From them—some fleeing, some turning back again, some gazing on, and some standing fast—there arose a most terrible din.

sanskrit: śūrāṇāṃ harṣajanano bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhanaḥ dyāvāpṛthivyor vivaraṃ pūrayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: Begetting joy in the brave and swelling the fear of the timid, it filled on every side the gulf between heaven and earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar api droṇo nāma viśrāvayan yudhi akarod raudram ātmānaṃ kirañ śaraśataiḥ parān
english: Then once again Droṇa, proclaiming his name aloud in the battle, made himself terrible, scattering hundreds of shafts upon the foe.

sanskrit: sa tathā tāny anīkāni pāṇḍaveyasya dhīmataḥ kālavan nyavadhīd droṇo yuveva sthaviro balī
english: Thus did the mighty Droṇa slay those divisions of the wise Pāṇḍava like Time itself—an old man, yet as a youth.

sanskrit: utkṛtya ca śirāṃsy ugro bāhūn api sabhūṣaṇān kṛtvā śūnyān rathopasthān udakrośan mahārathaḥ
english: And the fierce mighty car-warrior, lopping off heads and arms still bedecked with ornaments, leaving the chariot-seats empty, raised a great shout.

sanskrit: tasya harṣapraṇādena bāṇavegena cābhibho prākampanta raṇe yodhā gāvaḥ śītārditā iva
english: At his shout of joy and the rush of his arrows, O lord, the warriors trembled in the battle like cattle tormented by the cold.

sanskrit: droṇasya rathaghoṣeṇa maurvīniṣpeṣaṇena ca dhanuḥśabdena cākāśe śabdaḥ samabhavan mahān
english: From the roar of Droṇa's chariot, the lashing of his bowstring, and the twang of his bow, a great sound arose in the sky.

sanskrit: athāsya bahuśo bāṇā niścarantaḥ sahasraśaḥ vyāpya sarvā diśaḥ petur gajāśvarathapattiṣu
english: Then his arrows, issuing forth in their thousands, filling all the quarters, fell upon elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: taṃ kārmukamahāvegam astrajvalitapāvakam droṇam āsādayāṃ cakruḥ pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: Upon that Droṇa, mighty in the speed of his bow, his weapons blazing like kindled fire, the Pāñcālas with the Pāṇḍavas closed in.

sanskrit: tān vai sarathahastyaśvān prāhiṇod yamasādanam droṇo 'cireṇākaroc ca mahīṃ śoṇitakardamām
english: Them, with their chariots, elephants, and horses, Droṇa sent to the abode of Yama, and in no long while made the earth a mire of blood.

sanskrit: tanvatā paramāstrāṇi śarān satatam asyatā droṇena vihitaṃ dikṣu bāṇajālam adṛśyata
english: As he plied his supreme weapons and ceaselessly loosed his shafts, a net of arrows woven by Droṇa was seen across the quarters of the sky.

sanskrit: padātiṣu rathāśveṣu vāraṇeṣu ca sarvaśaḥ tasya vidyud ivābhreṣu caran ketur adṛśyata
english: Ranging over the foot-soldiers, the chariots and horses, and the elephants on every side, his banner was seen like lightning amid the clouds.

sanskrit: sa kekayānāṃ pravarāṃś ca pañca; pāñcālarājaṃ ca śaraiḥ pramṛdya yudhiṣṭhirānīkam adīnayodhī; droṇo 'bhyayāt kārmukabāṇapāṇiḥ
english: Having crushed with his shafts the five chief warriors of the Kekayas and the king of the Pāñcālas, Droṇa, that undaunted fighter, bow and arrow in hand, advanced upon Yudhiṣṭhira's division.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmasenaś ca dhanaṃjayaś ca; śineś ca naptā drupadātmajaś ca śaibyātmajaḥ kāśipatiḥ śibiś ca; hṛṣṭā nadanto vyakirañ śaraughaiḥ
english: At him Bhīmasena and Dhanaṃjaya, the grandson of Śini, the son of Drupada, the son of Śaibyā, the lord of Kāśi, and Śibi, exulting and roaring aloud, hurled torrents of arrows.

sanskrit: teṣām atho droṇadhanurvimuktāḥ; patatriṇaḥ kāñcanacitrapuṅkhāḥ bhittvā śarīrāṇi gajāśvayūnāṃ; jagmur mahīṃ śoṇitadigdhavājāḥ
english: Then the feathered shafts loosed from Droṇa's bow, their golden, many-hued nocks bright, piercing the bodies of their elephants, horses, and men, passed into the earth, their plumes drenched with blood.

sanskrit: sā yodhasaṃghaiś ca rathaiś ca bhūmiḥ; śarair vibhinnair gajavājibhiś ca pracchādyamānā patitair babhūva; samantato dyaur iva kālameghaiḥ
english: That earth, strewn over with hosts of fallen warriors and chariots, with shattered arrows and elephants and horses, became as the sky overspread on every side with the clouds of doom.

sanskrit: śaineyabhīmārjunavāhinīpāñ; śaibyābhimanyū saha kāśirājñā anyāṃś ca vīrān samare pramṛdnād; droṇaḥ sutānāṃ tava bhūtikāmaḥ
english: The leaders of the hosts of Sātyaki, Bhīma, and Arjuna; Śaibya and Abhimanyu, together with the king of Kāśi; and other heroes besides—Droṇa, desiring the welfare of your sons, crushed them in the fight.

sanskrit: etāni cānyāni ca kauravendra; karmāṇi kṛtvā samare mahātmā pratāpya lokān iva kālasūryo; droṇo gataḥ svargam ito hi rājan
english: Having wrought these deeds and others in the battle, O lord of the Kurus, the high-souled Droṇa, scorching the worlds as the sun of doom, departed hence to heaven, O king.

sanskrit: evaṃ rukmarathaḥ śūro hatvā śatasahasraśaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ raṇe yodhān pārṣatena nipātitaḥ
english: Thus the hero of the golden chariot, having slain the warriors of the Pāṇḍavas in the battle by the hundred thousand, was struck down by the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇīm abhyadhikāṃ śūrāṇām anivartinām nihatya paścād dhṛtimān agacchat paramāṃ gatim
english: Having slain more than a full akṣauhiṇī of heroes who never turned back, that steadfast one thereafter attained the supreme goal.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavaiḥ saha pāñcālair aśivaiḥ krūrakarmabhiḥ hato rukmaratho rājan kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram
english: By the Pāñcālas, together with the Pāṇḍavas—malign and cruel of deed—was the hero of the golden chariot slain, O king, after he had wrought a most arduous deed.

sanskrit: tato ninādo bhūtānām ākāśe samajāyata sainyānāṃ ca tato rājann ācārye nihate yudhi
english: Then a cry of all beings arose in the sky, and likewise of the armies, O king, when the preceptor was slain in the battle.
